scenes.headline: The 1994 Wall Street Bonus Dilemma
scenes.stat_label: SAFE SIX-FIGURE BONUS VS GARAGE BOOKSTORE
bullets: Age 30 VP at Wall Street firm D.E. Shaw
Quitting mid-year meant forfeiting a huge annual bonus
scenes.narration: In 1994, a thirty-year-old Wall Street vice president had to decide whether to give up a massive mid-year bonus to sell books on an obscure new network called the internet.

scenes.headline: Project Your Mind Forward to Age 80
bullets: Step outside short-term salary noise and social approval
Minimize total lifelong regrets from your 80th birthday
scenes.narration: His boss warned him not to leave a great job. So Jeff Bezos pictured himself at age eighty looking back on his life, aiming to minimize the total regrets he would carry.

scenes.headline: Trying & Failing vs Never Trying at All
scenes.left_body: Forfeiting one annual bonus, awkward failure, bruised pride
scenes.right_body: 0% regret for trying and failing -> 100% haunting regret for never trying
scenes.narration: At eighty, he knew he would never regret missing one Wall Street bonus, and he would not even regret trying and failing. The one thing that would haunt him forever was never trying.

scenes.headline: 75% of Deep Life Regrets Are Inactions
scenes.stat_subtext: Mistakes hurt briefly in the present; unlived paths ache for decades
scenes.narration: Cornell psychologist Thomas Gilovich confirmed why in 1995: seventy-five percent of enduring human regrets come from paths we were too cautious to test, never attempts that fell short.

scenes.headline: Let Your 80-Year-Old Self Break the Tie
scenes.stat_label: IGNORE TEMPORARY PRIDE - OPTIMIZE FOR AGE 80
bullets: Cap your downside so survival is protected
Then take the swing your older self will thank you for
